overall: Thursday in Washington, DC is expected to bring dangerously hot conditions with full sunshine and a NWS-forecast high near 104°F, accompanied by heat index values potentially reaching 109–112°F. An Extreme Heat Warning is in effect through July 3, reflecting what could be one of the most intense heat days of the summer season. West winds of 2–8 mph will provide little relief, making outdoor exposure hazardous for extended periods.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is notably poor, with ECMWF being the warmest contributor at an expected TMAX of ~99.8°F and a 33% chance of reaching ≥100°F, while HRRR sits at ~97.6°F and WEATHER_COM at ~94.2°F. GFS (~87.4°F) and NBM (~81.8°F) are significant outliers on the cool side, and GEM shows essentially zero probability for the ≥100°F bucket — this wide spread is a meaningful caution flag despite the NWS's confident 104°F headline.
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble model expects a TMAX of approximately 97.7°F, considerably below the NWS's 104°F call, while the prior day's observed high of 97.0°F provides a warm baseline. In the active even-bucket market, the ≥100°F bucket leads at 23.6% — no other bucket comes close — but this is a Tier 2 signal with ~52% expected accuracy, reflecting meaningful uncertainty from the wide model spread. Balancing the NWS forecast, the ECMWF's ~99.8°F estimate, the Extreme Heat Warning context, and the ensemble model's more conservative 97.7°F, the most likely outcome is a high in the upper 90s to near 100°F, with a real but minority chance of cracking 100°F.
